sections.html:
The Tax Office has two departments, both at 227 N. Main Street in Raeford. The Assessor lists, appraises and assesses all taxable property. Collections bills and collects tax on real estate, personal property and delinquent motor vehicles.

The mailing address is PO Box 1557, Raeford, NC 28376, and the phone is 910-875-8751. The county's roll covers about 28,000 parcels of land, 700 businesses and 40,000 motor vehicles across roughly 390 square miles of land.

For context on pricing, Hoke has grown from 52,082 people at the 2020 count to an estimate of 56,939 in July 2025, with 22,440 housing units. Owners occupy 73.0 percent of homes, and the median owned home is valued at $219,300. Builders took out 558 permits in 2025.

sections.h2: Rates and fees on the bill
sections.html:
A bill is built from the county rate, any city rate, a fire district rate and a solid waste fee. Rates apply to each $100 of value, and properties inside a city do not pay the fire district tax or the solid waste fee.

Sample Hoke County bill lines
Line on the billRate or fee
Hoke County rate.73 per $100 of value
City of Raeford rate.48 per $100 of value
North Raeford fire district rate.10 per $100 of value
Solid waste fee$130.00 per unit in the sample bill

Fire district rates differ by district. Ask the Tax Office for the sheet that lists the district for your parcel, and confirm the current Raeford rate if the house is inside city limits.

The last countywide revaluation took effect January 1, 2022, with notices going to all taxpayers on February 3, 2022. The next is set for January 1, 2030, and work starts two years before.

State law, G.S. 105-286, requires reappraisal at least every eight years. Until then, your real property value stays tied to the January 1, 2022 market level unless you add improvements or the parcel changes. Ask the assessor how a sale price compares with the 2022 value on your parcel.

An appraisal sets each owner's share of the taxes that support schools, roads, parks, public health, libraries, police and fire protection. What you pay depends on your value and the rates set each year by elected county and city or town officials.

File the Notice of Appeal of Assessment with the Tax Assessor before the equalization board adjourns. The date is advertised in the local paper and online, and the assessor's office can confirm it.

  • Use one form per parcel, signed by the owner or a representative (an attorney, or an attorney in fact holding a power of attorney when the owner is not a corporation).
  • Evidence can be an appraisal, sales of similar properties, income and expense statements or replacement cost. Send copies with the form.
  • The owner must show the value substantially exceeds true market value on the January 1, 2022 valuation date.
  • The board sets a hearing date and tells you. You can attend or send counsel.

An appraisal you already gave in an informal appeal need not be sent again. After the county board, the next stop is the Property Tax Commission, with written notice due 30 days after the decision is mailed. See G.S. 105-290.

September 1 is the due date. Under G.S. 105-360, paying before January 6 costs face value. From then until February 1 a charge of 2 percent applies, followed by three quarters of a percent per month.

You can pay online, and Collections answers billing questions. For mail, the USPS postmark date counts, so keep the envelope. State law lets a county offer prepayment discounts, so ask whether Hoke has one.

Under G.S. 105-355, unpaid tax attaches to the parcel as a lien from the listing date, and the county can enforce it by foreclosure filed where the land lies. A sale is a public auction at the courthouse door. Someone who redeems before confirmation pays the tax plus penalties, interest and costs. See G.S. 105-374.

North Carolina offers an elderly or disabled exclusion, a disabled veteran exclusion and a circuit breaker deferral. An owner may take only one. The county assessor takes the Form AV-9 filing.

The 2026 thresholds are $38,800 for the base income limit and $58,200 for the circuit breaker's upper tier. Filings are accepted through June 1 before the tax year. A transfer of the property triggers the deferred tax under the circuit breaker, so mention it to your attorney before you list. See NCDOR Form AV-9.

sections.h2: Handling the tax bill when you sell
sections.html:
Request a payoff from Collections that covers this year and earlier years. Because the lien dates from the listing date, an unpaid current-year bill must be cleared at closing.

  • Have the closing attorney pay taxes from proceeds.
  • Look for a fire district tax and a solid waste fee on the bill if the house sits outside Raeford.
  • Confirm any exclusion filing is current before the sale.
  • Keep your 2022 value notice handy for buyers who ask.

Call Collections at 910-875-8751 early. A payoff quoted a few weeks before closing may need a refresh, since the figure changes once penalties start in January. A cash buyer can close on a short timeline, but the tax payoff still comes out of your proceeds, so line it up before the closing date is set.

sections.h2: Reading your bill before you list
sections.html:
Pull out last year's bill and find each line. The county rate applies to every parcel. A Raeford rate shows up only for houses inside the city. A fire district rate and the solid waste fee show up only outside city limits, and the district depends on where the parcel sits. If a line looks wrong, call the Tax Office before a buyer's attorney spots it.

Then look at the value. Because the 2022 revaluation set values to the market as of January 1, 2022, your assessed value may sit well away from what a buyer will pay today. That gap is normal and is not grounds for an appeal on its own. An appeal has to show the value was too high on the 2022 date, not that the market has moved since.

Here is how the year runs for an owner who plans to sell. Bills are due September 1. Pay by January 6 and nothing extra is added. After that comes the 2 percent charge, and three quarters of a percent more each month. Unpaid tax becomes a lien from the listing date, so by the time a contract is signed the buyer's side will ask for the account to be paid or cleared at closing.

Gather your parcel information, your latest bill, any exclusion filing and your 2022 value notice before the first showing. Having them ready lets Collections quote a payoff quickly and keeps the closing from slipping over a tax question.

faqs.q: Where is the Hoke County Tax Office?
faqs.a: Both the Assessor and Collections are at 227 N. Main Street in Raeford. The mailing address is PO Box 1557, Raeford, NC 28376, and the phone is 910-875-8751.

faqs.q: When is the next Hoke County revaluation?
faqs.a: January 1, 2030. The last one took effect January 1, 2022, with notices mailed February 3, 2022, and work begins two years before the effective date.

faqs.q: What is the Hoke County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county's sample bill shows a county rate of .73 per $100, a Raeford rate of .48 and a North Raeford fire district rate of .10. A solid waste fee can apply outside city limits, so ask for the current rate sheet.

faqs.q: What do I file to contest a value?
faqs.a: A Notice of Appeal of Assessment for each parcel, filed with the Tax Assessor before the equalization board adjourns, with evidence such as appraisals or comparable sales. The adjournment date is advertised in the newspaper and on the county website.

faqs.q: Does Hoke County have a fire district tax?
faqs.a: Yes. A fire district rate is charged on top of the county rate, based on the district where the property sits. City properties do not pay it.
